recoverable_gpu_hours.basis: Computed by the dashboard's selection/adjustment engine (dashboard/server/model/overlap.ts) with every GPU-hour opportunity selected. Findings are grouped by dedup key (job / node / user), each key's claim is capped at the real allocated hours of what it covers (job's gpu_hours from data/prepped/jobs.parquet; node's and user's totals likewise), then every adjusted claim is re-attributed to the jobs it covers and capped again at the job grain so the total can never exceed the cluster's 594,004 GPU-hour allocation. The adjusted, reconciled total is 447,210 GPU-hours split by impact kind: consumed 254,209, unused_capacity 122,431, lost 64,913, degraded 5,656. Low = sum of kind hours x the conservative end of the recovery factors in dashboard/server/model/catalog.ts (unused_capacity 0.50, lost 0.30, consumed 0.15, degraded 0.05); high = the optimistic end (0.80 / 0.60 / 0.40 / 0.25). The interval is a SCENARIO: its ends are two defensible recovery assumptions, not a statistical spread; the factors themselves are editorial judgment, disclosed on every card in the dashboard. Cross-scope overlap (a user-scope finding covers hours that job-scope findings also claim) is reconciled at the job grain, not summed.

recoverable_usd.basis: Same engine and selection as recoverable_gpu_hours, priced at the official price book (usd_per_gpu_hour = 2.50, version 2026-Q3). recoverable_gpu_hours x 2.50 equals this interval by construction. Point is the interval midpoint. Against the baseline spend of $1,485,009.60 the interval is 20.0%-40.4% of spend.

cancelled_rationale: CANCELLED (203,930 GPU-hours, 34.3% of allocated) is treated as deliberate early stopping, not waste: users cancel runs that look wrong, which is good practice (docs/traps.md). The dashboard's efficiency states for teams exclude CANCELLED from failure rates, and no recovery factor is applied to cancelled hours. Counting them as waste would roughly double the headline; we chose the conservative reading and show CANCELLED separately everywhere.

incident_degraded_gpu_hours.basis: Sum of metadata.impact_gpu_hours over the 121 rules::filesystem-latency-degraded findings (impact_kind = degraded, node scope). Verified live via POST /v1/causal for finding de0755a6-6911-5c23-96ff-9fc8d47ebd1e: root cause pvc/scratch-lustre-02, filesystem p99 latency rose 40.1x, affecting 121 nodes, culprit score 0.88. Degraded means work continued slower, not destroyed, so these hours are not claimed as recoverable savings at face value. Single point estimate on purpose: 'degraded' hours have no defensible spread beyond the recovery scenario, and the honest move is not to invent one. Note: this incident is synthetic (metadata.synthetic = true), injected by the challenge - one incident, not 121 problems.

hardware_attributable_rationale: Counted: (1) 10 jobs that ENDED in NODE_FAIL - the scheduler's own record that a machine died under them (docs/traps.md: 18,587 failures, 10 end in NODE_FAIL); (2) 140 jobs on r216287-n200569 that failed with exit status 135 (SIGBUS) during 2026-02-27 to 2026-03-07, when that machine broke for about a week without ever being marked down. Verified live via POST /v1/causal for the rules::node-hardware-fault finding: 3 different people crashed with SIGBUS on this machine, 140 of 144 jobs failed, and none of the three produces exit status 135 anywhere else (0 occurrences across 1,427 + 1,544 + 946 jobs elsewhere) - causal confidence 1.0, the machine is the culprit. Excluded: the other 21 jobs that hit a node failure at some point but ended differently (6 completed after a requeue, the rest ended in other terminal states) - their final outcome is not attributable to hardware alone; and any fault the scheduler never recorded at all. The two counted groups are disjoint (the SIGBUS machine was never marked down, so none of its failures carry NODE_FAIL).

card_imbalance_gpu_hours.basis: Sum of metadata.impact_gpu_hours over the 689 rules::gpu-imbalance findings (job scope, impact_kind unused_capacity): 14,559 GPU-hours held by GPUs inside multi-GPU jobs that never drove them. low/high apply the unused_capacity recovery assumption (50-80%, dashboard/server/model/catalog.ts) - a scenario interval, not a statistical one. 48 teams affected across 200 machines.

card_imbalance_rationale: Used the detector's own per-job findings rather than re-pivoting gpus.parquet: the rule reports the idle GPU-hours per job directly (metadata.impact_gpu_hours, impact_kind = unused_capacity). The deck card opp:rules::gpu-imbalance shows $18,199-$29,118 potential at $2.50/GPU-h.
notes: Every number in this file comes from the dashboard engine (dashboard/server/) reading the data generated by the official pipeline (make prep, make generate), or from live API calls recorded during preparation. The dashboard and this file share the same adjustment engine, so a judge can reproduce any figure: GET /api/context, GET /api/deck, POST /api/selection/adjust on http://localhost:3000. node_triage is deliberately omitted: the 113 rules::node-elevated-failure-rate findings were not individually triaged.
